title: The Mall World Basketball 🏀 Stadium
content: This morning, after I woke up 15 minutes before the alarm on my wife’s phone went off, I sleepily turned over and quickly fell into a new Mall World dream. We were sitting at a professional basketball game, myself and a woman I’ve come to recognize in several dreams, but I still don’t have a name for. Usually I see her in the 1960’s early 70’s time period - sometimes she’s a governess for a pair of siblings, other times she’s the teacher at a school. We watched the game till the end, she didn’t quite understand the game and would lean over to politely ask me questions. After a while, she became mesmerized by the action, especially the dunks and long three pointers. Our team won (naturally) and we left with the crowd outside. The stadium concourse was futuristic, painted in a light yellow cream color and had no sharp angles reminiscent of the “Flintstones”. The area was lit up brightly, but the fixtures were hidden (this is when I became Lucid) my mind is wandering trying to figure out how the lights work. My companion tells me she wants to return to the hotel, I agree - sensing her uneasiness in large crowds. We head up the escalator, noticing we can see the stadium floor where some players were still on the court talking and taking shots instead of leaving for the night. “Don’t they have to go home?” My companion asked innocently “Yes” I said, pointing out the coach was out there too, perhaps having a briefing and cooling down after the excitement of the game. She was totally innocent, and inquisitive, as if she didn’t belong in our timeline. We kept going up the escalator several flights because the Hotel we were staying in was connected to the stadium. I realized she was wearing her usual clothes from her time period - she was a slightly built African American woman dressed like Jaqueline Kennedy, demure and educated I felt like I was her chaperone in Mall World, showing her a good time and taking her safely back to her room. Dinner wasn’t discussed so that part wasn’t relevant. I was pulled out of the dream when my wife turned over to stop the alarm on her phone - 15 minutes later.
